figures.title: Where a program's data lives: stack and heap
figures.description: Two columns. The left column is the stack, containing three frames for main, printReport, and percentageOf, with a note that frames appear and vanish automatically as functions are entered and left. The right column is the heap, containing two blocks obtained with new, with a note that heap blocks stay until something releases them. An arrow runs from a pointer variable inside the main frame to one of the heap blocks, labelled scheme underscore. A caption records that the stack is managed for you and the heap is not, which is the entire subject of the chapter.
